manifest.name: dsh-taskforce
manifest.description: Multi-agent orchestration plugin for DeepSeek Harness: task graph, context routing, structured reports, review loop

readme.text:
[English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

Multi-agent orchestration plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

Splits long tasks across multiple purpose-built agents so no single agent's context
accumulates the whole task: a planner decomposes work into a task graph, each worker
runs in a **fresh one-shot context** holding only what its task needs, and workers
return **structured reports** instead of transcripts.
Core loop: `plan → dispatch (parallel) → structured reports → review → pass | redo`.

Status: **full loop + cross-restart recovery + Web panel + adoption prompt** —
plan → dispatch → structured reports → review (pass/fail) → reroute → re-dispatch
→ finalize all work; on top of that the task graph survives a restart (the host's
own log is replayed into it) and the conversation composer shows an orchestration
panel — both verified live. A system-prompt section exists to get the pipeline
**chosen** for large requests that never name it: it was verified that the section
reaches the model, positioned after the workflow and subagent sections, but the
behavioural half — whether the agent actually calls `orchestrate_plan` when nobody
names it — is **not verified yet** (the run that would settle it was blocked on an
invalid API key). State is keyed per conversation; worker tool access is
whitelist-constrained; worker profiles are configurable. 16 offline test groups
pass (CI runs them on every push/PR). See `../DESIGN.zh.md`.

> **Naming**: the repository and the local folder keep the historical name
> `dsh-orchestra`; the GitHub repo and the package are `dsh-taskforce`. The tool
> names `orchestrate_*`, the service name `orchestra` and the projection key
> `orchestraGraph` are frozen **on purpose** — they appear in the host's own
> tool-call log, so renaming them would break recovery for sessions recorded
> before the change. Do not "tidy" them up.

From a local checkout (run `pnpm install` inside this directory after cloning —
the bundle has one npm dependency; see [Compatibility](#compatibility) for the
dsh versions this was verified against):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LiSheng5/dsh-taskforce.git
pnpm install
dsh plugin --profile web add <path-to>/dsh-taskforce
```

`<path-to>` must be an absolute path. `dsh plugin add` also accepts git specs
directly (`github:LiSheng5/dsh-taskforce`) — pnpm then resolves the dependency at
install time.

**Using the desktop app rather than the CLI?** It ships its own launcher
(`resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd` on Windows) and manages the `desktop`
profile exclusively: booting or dumping that profile from the CLI is refused,
installing into it is not.

```sh
"<DeepSeek Harness>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add <path-to>\dsh-taskforce
```

The app's own sidebar **Plugins** page installs the same way — a registry name,
a git address, a tarball or an absolute local path — and the bundle is enabled by
default. Restart the app to load it.

| dsh version | status |
|---|---|
| `0.1.7-rc.2` | developed against; full loop, restart recovery and Web panel verified |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | the desktop app's runtime; install, mount and prompt assembly verified headless (the section renders where it should, tool text reaches the model) — the full orchestration loop and the Web panel have not been re-run on it |

dsh is a developer preview and officially announces breaking changes. After
upgrading dsh, run the offline regression suite once — it needs no dsh, no API
key, no network:

```sh
node test/local-loop.mjs
```

The same suite runs in CI on every push and pull request
(`.github/workflows/offline-regression.yml`, Node 20 / 22 / 24), so "run it once
after upgrading dsh" and "CI blocks regressions" are the same command.

Upgrading from a version that predates the restart-recovery fix? Conversations
it touched need a one-time repair — see
[Upgrading from a version that predates the fix](#upgrading-from-a-version-that-predates-the-fix).

A composition without `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` loses exactly one thing:
the prompt section that makes the pipeline get chosen on its own. Every tool
still works when it is named explicitly.

This plugin spawns **real sub-agents with real powers**: file reads/writes and
shell access inside the session workspace, bounded by each worker profile's
tool restrictions. Read [dsh's own SAFETY notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
before running orchestrations on workspaces you care about, keep the per-task
timeout and attempt caps enabled, and treat worker reports as claims — that is
what the reviewer is for.

Workers also lose the host's agent-plane **control tools** by default
(`send_message`, `interrupt_agent`, `list_agents`, `subagent`, `subagent_fork`):
`send_message` would post a worker's text straight into the **orchestrator's
session**, which is exactly what this plugin exists to prevent, and the others
let a worker disturb its parent or start more agents. This list was calibrated
by measurement (a real researcher worker reported exactly these tools); set
`denyControlPlane: false` to keep them.

```
index.js            plugin entry: name / inject / apply
client.js           browser half: the panel above the composer (lazy __ModuleLoader__ factory)
cordis.patch.yml    bundle patch inserted into the profile composition
src/protocol.js     Task / Report / Verdict JSON schemas (host JSON-Schema subset)

The graph lives in memory, keyed per conversation, so a restart loses it. What
brings it back is the session log the host already keeps:

- dsh logs every tool call as `tool/call` (full arguments) and `tool/result`
  (rendered output), so orchestration state is durable in the host's own
  vocabulary — the plugin writes no session events of its own.
- The plugin registers an `orchestraGraph` session projection (under
  `ctx.inject([...])`, so a composition without the projection registry is
  unaffected) that purely folds those events into the task graph, and loads it
  the first time a fresh process touches the conversation.
- **A call's effect lands when its result settles.** The host writes
  `tool/call` before the tool body runs, so applying eagerly would apply the
  call being executed right now a second time. A dispatch that was cut short by
  a restart is therefore never half-applied either: its task stays where the
  orchestrator last saw it — ready to run again.
- Without the projection service the plugin simply runs in-memory, as before.
- Conversations recorded **before the `✓ <id> — <detail>` render contract**
  (early builds) recover their plan, attempts, verdicts and finalized flag but
  not their dispatch outcomes: the old digest carries no success marker, and
  inventing one would be worse than leaving
`orchestrate_status` answers with the recovered graph after a restart.

readme.section: Upgrading from a version that predates the fix
readme.text:
Early versions appended their own event types, which made those conversations
**unloadable after a dsh restart** (`contains event type "orchestra/graph" …
refusing to interpret the log`). The repair script adds the harness's own
compatibility marker (`ignorable`) so they load again, backing up first:

readme.section: Upgrading from a version that predates the fix
readme.text:
```sh
node scripts/repair-session-logs.mjs --dry-run   # report first
node scripts/repair-session-logs.mjs             # repair (self-checked, backup kept)
node scripts/repair-session-logs.mjs --restore   # undo
```

Conversations that have an orchestration show a panel above the composer (a
conversation that never planned anything renders nothing at all):

```
▾ ▣ orchestra #1 · 1/2 · review 1 PASS
  ─────────────────────────────────────
  ✓ t1  researcher  completed  att 1
     read package.json — name dsh-taskforce, version 0.1.0 …

- It reads the **wire view** of the same `orchestraGraph` projection
  (`client.js` calls `useProjection('orchestraGraph')`), so it shows exactly
  what `orchestrate_status` reports, updates itself as events arrive, and after
  a restart shows the recovered graph.
- Only ids, agent types, statuses, attempts, readiness, report summaries,
  diagnostics and issue counts cross to the browser; worker personas stay
  host-side.
- The browser half is a **build-free plain script** (`client.js`, declared by
  `dsh.client.platform=web` with `immediately`). It inherits the host theme via
  `currentColor` and pulls in no stylesheet or third-party dependency.
- Uninstalling the plugin removes the panel with its loader row; the rest of the
  conversation UI is untouched.

The plugin also registers a **system-prompt section** (`tool:orchestrate_plan`,
order 2810) so the host agent reaches for the pipeline on a large request it was
never told to name — measured behaviour before this was `todo_write` plus doing
the work itself. It follows the host's own convention (workflow owns order 2600,
subagent 2800), is registered under `ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], …)` so a
composition without that service merely loses the advocacy, and renders as an
empty string for any agent that cannot see `orchestrate_plan` — which is every
worker, because a spawned child's persona only shadows the deployment persona
and global sections do reach it. All model-facing text lives in `src/prompts.js`.

- `orchestrate_plan` — submit the task graph (mission_brief + tasks); validates
  fail-loud and returns the ready set. Its description is where the
  decomposition rules live: workstreams are how you *find* the cut but must be
  restated as file ownership, task counts scale with the request, the
  parallel-writer hazard, two worked skeletons, and the anti-patterns.
- `orchestrate_status` — compact one-row-per-task view plus dispatchable ids,
  and the diagnostic for tasks that failed without producing a report.
- `orchestrate_dispatch` — spawn ready tasks as isolated one-shot workers,
  block until they settle, return one report digest per task (≤4 concurrent).
- `orchestrate_review` — run the reviewer over the reports; returns a verdict.
- `orchestrate_reroute` — send review issues back to workers with guidance.
- `orchestrate_finalize` — record the delivery summary and lock the graph.
- `orchestra_ping` — liveness probe.

**The orchestrator writes per-task personas itself**: each task in a plan may
carry a `persona` field — a role definition A tailors to that task ("你是数据库
迁移专家，只改 SQL 文件"). It becomes the worker's primary system prompt, layered
above the profile's `discipline` (non-negotiable constraints that A cannot
override: researchers don't write, reviewers don't fix, …). `model` and
`reasoning_effort` are likewise per-task fields A sets at plan time.

Two more ways to tune what each worker role is like — both take effect after
restarting the dsh process:

1. **Edit `src/profiles.js` directly.** Each role has `role` (identity line),
   `discipline` (permanent constraints), `effort` (`off|low|high|max`), and
   `toolDenyPatterns` — regexes matched (case-insensitively) against the host's
   global tool names to hard-restrict that role's tools.

2. **Config overrides (no code edit).** Add a `config:` block to the plugin
   entry in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (e.g.
   `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
   - id: dsh-taskforce
     name: dsh-taskforce
     config:
       taskTimeoutMs: 1200000

Config `role`/`discipline`/`model`/`effort` replace the builtin values;
   `toolDenyPatterns` are concatenated with the builtin ones. Engine knobs:
   `provider` (default `spawn`), `maxConcurrentWorkers` (4), `maxAttempts` (3),
   `maxReviewRounds` (3), `taskTimeoutMs` (600000).

The orchestrator is not limited to the four builtin worker types. In a plan it
may **declare new worker types** — `orchestrate_plan` accepts a `workers` field
where A programs one agent spec per type:

```jsonc
"workers": [
  {
    "type": "ui-builder",
    "role": "你是界面构建师，专注像素级还原。",      // identity (required for new types)

- Tasks then reference `"agent_type": "ui-builder"`. Shadowing a builtin type
  (`"type": "coder"`, no role) replaces only the parts it names.
- The layering stays: a task-level `persona` still layers above the declared
  role, and the declared `discipline` is always appended — A cannot write it away.
- The review loop is not reprogrammable from plans: the reviewer always runs on
  the operator-configured profile.
- Engine-level guarantees are unaffected: orchestration tools are always denied
  to workers, delegation depth prevents grandchild spawning, tasks are one-shot
  isolated sessions.

- **Hand-built tool definitions, near-zero imports**: tool definitions match
  what `defineTool` compiles to; the only dependency is the npm-published
  `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` for the Config schema, so pnpm-local-path
  installs stay trivial.
- **Context isolation**: workers are spawned (never forked) one-shot subagents;
  upstream information travels only as structured reports, never as history.
- **Prompt text is layered and frozen**: a system-prompt section says WHEN to
  enter the pipeline, the `orchestrate_plan` description says HOW to decompose,
  and the parameter descriptions carry per-field rules — all of it in
  `src/prompts.js` as module constants, because sections and tool schemas are
  re-sent on every request and byte-stable text is what keeps the provider's
  prefix cache reusable. Both texts reach the orchestrator only: a worker gets
  an empty section and never sees the planner's schema, so `TASK_ITEM_SCHEMA`
  wording costs nothing per worker turn. The offline suite enforces a character
  budget on each, so the per-request cost cannot silently grow.
- **Decompose by deliverable, never by role**: the planner guidance was settled
  against a survey of four other

DeepSeek Harness（dsh）的多智能体编排插件。

把长任务拆给多个目标明确的智能体，避免任何单个智能体的上下文累积整个任务：规划者把工作分解为任务图，
每个 worker 在**全新的一次性上下文**中运行，只拿到自己那块任务需要的信息，并以**结构化报告**回传结果。

核心闭环：`计划 → 派发 → 结构化报告 → 审核 → 通过 | 重做`。

状态：**闭环 + 跨重启恢复 + Web 面板 + 自动触发提示段**——计划 → 派发 → 结构化报告 → 审核（通过/失败）→
回退 → 再派发 → 收尾，全部跑通；**跨重启恢复**（重放宿主日志重建任务图）与会话输入框上方的
**Web 编排面板** 都已真机验收。另有让流水线被**自动选中**的系统提示段：已实测该段确实进入模型上下文、
且落在 workflow 段与 subagent 段之后，但行为层的另一半——**不点名时 agent 是否真的会去调
`orchestrate_plan`**——**尚未验收**（那次实验被无效的 API Key 挡在 401）。
离线回归 16 组全绿（CI 每次 push / PR 都会跑）。设计文档见（本地）`../DESIGN.zh.md`。

> **命名**：仓库与本地目录沿用历史名 `dsh-orchestra`，而 GitHub 仓库与包名是 `dsh-taskforce`——照路径操作没问题。
> 工具名 `orchestrate_*`、服务名 `orchestra`、投影键 `orchestraGraph` 是**刻意冻结**的：它们出现在宿主自己的
> 工具调用日志里，改名会让改动之前的会话恢复不出来，所以不要"顺手统一"。

从本地目录安装（克隆后在本目录内执行 `pnpm install`——本插件有一个 npm 依赖；验证过哪些
dsh 版本见[兼容性](#兼容性)）：

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LiSheng5/dsh-taskforce.git
pnpm install
dsh plugin --profile web add <本插件所在绝对路径>
```

`<本插件所在绝对路径>` 必须是绝对路径。`dsh plugin add` 也直接接受 git 形式
（`github:LiSheng5/dsh-taskforce`）——依赖由 pnpm 在安装时解析。

**用的是桌面版而不是 CLI？** 桌面版自带启动器（Windows 上是
`resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd`），并且**独占管理** `desktop` profile：用 CLI 去
boot / dump 这个 profile 会被拒绝，但往里装插件不会。

```sh
"<DeepSeek Harness>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add <本插件所在绝对路径>
```

应用自己的侧边栏 **Plugins** 页做的是同一件事——接受 registry 包名、git 地址、tarball
或本地绝对路径——装完默认就是启用状态。重启应用即生效。

| dsh 版本 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| `0.1.7-rc.2` | 开发与验证基准：全闭环、跨重启恢复、Web 面板均真机验收过 |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | 桌面版自带运行时；安装、挂载、提示词组装已 headless 实测（提示段渲染在预期位置、工具文案确实到达模型），**编排全闭环与 Web 面板尚未在此版本重跑** |

dsh 目前是开发者预览版，官方明示会出现破坏性变更。升级 dsh 后先跑一次离线回归
（不需要 dsh、不需要 API Key、不需要网络）：

```sh
node test/local-loop.mjs
```

同一套回归在 CI 里每次 push / PR 都会自动跑（`.github/workflows/offline-regression.yml`，
Node 20 / 22 / 24 三档）——所以"升级 dsh 后本地跑一次"和"CI 挡住回归"用的是同一条命令。

没有 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` 的组装只少一样东西：让流水线被**自动选中**的那段
提示。点名调用时，所有工具照常工作。

readme.section: 升级自早于本次修复的版本
readme.text:
早期版本会向会话日志写入自定义事件类型，导致**这些会话在 dsh 重启后无法加载**
（`contains event type "orchestra/graph" … refusing to interpret the log`）。修复脚本会
给这些行补上官方兼容标记（`ignorable`），恢复会话可用（原文件自动备份）：

```sh
node scripts/repair-session-logs.mjs --dry-run   # 先看影响范围
node scripts/repair-session-logs.mjs             # 执行修复（含自检与备份）
node scripts/repair-session-logs.mjs --restore   # 回滚
```

本插件会 spawn **有真实权限的子智能体**：在会话工作区内读写文件、执行 shell，受各 worker
profile 的工具限制约束。在重要工作区运行编排前，先阅读
[dsh 官方 SAFETY 说明](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)；
保持单任务超时与尝试次数上限开启；把 worker 的报告当作"声称"对待——这正是审核者存在的意义。

worker 默认还会被摘掉宿主的 agent-plane **控制面工具**（`send_message`、`interrupt_agent`、
`list_agents`、`subagent`、`subagent_fork`）：其中 `send_message` 能把 worker 的文字直接塞进
**编排者（A）的会话**，正是本插件要避免的事；其余几个让 worker 能打扰父代理或再拉代理。
这是实测校准出来的（真实 researcher worker 曾报出这些工具），嫌太严可以
`denyControlPlane: false` 关掉这一组。

```
dsh-taskforce/
├── package.json        # bundle 清单：dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client（web 面板）
├── cordis.patch.yml    # 组装补丁：把本插件插入 profile
├── index.js            # 插件入口：Config schema + apply()

- dsh 会把每次工具调用写成 `tool/call`（含完整参数）与 `tool/result`（含渲染结果），
  所以编排状态在会话日志里本来就是持久的。
- 插件注册一个 `orchestraGraph` Session projection（`ctx.sessionProjections.register`，
  在 `ctx.inject([...])` 下可选注册），纯函数折叠这些事件重建任务图；重启后第一次触达
  该会话时装载，于是 `orchestrate_status` 能报出重启前的任务图。
- **效果在 result 结算时才落地**：宿主在工具执行前就写 `tool/call`，急切应用会把"正在
  执行的那一次调用"应用两次；而被中断的派发（写日志的进程已死）因此不会污染恢复结果，
  对应任务保持可再次派发。
- 拿不到 projection 能力时静默降级为纯内存态（与早期版本行为一致），不影响插件加载。
- **渲染契约（`✓ <id> — <detail>`）之前**录下的会话能恢复计划、attempts、判定与 finalized
  标记，但恢复不出派发结果：旧摘要没有成功/失败标记，编造一个比"让任务停在原处"更糟。
  这类结果仍会消费掉自己的 pending 记录，因此不会被误报成"被重启打断"。

> 插件**不写自定义会话事件**：dsh 的持久化读路径拒绝加载含"本构建不认识且未标
> `ignorable`"事件类型的日志，而 `Session.append()` 无法写该标记——仓库外插件写自定义
> 事件会让整个会话在重启后无法加载。详见 `src/events.js` 顶部注释。

会话输入框上方会显示当前会话的编排面板（只在真的提交过计划后出现，普通会话完全无感）：

```
▾ ▣ orchestra #1 · 1/2 · review 1 PASS
  ─────────────────────────────────────
  ✓ t1  researcher  completed  att 1
    读 package.json 得到 name/version …

- 数据来自同一个 `orchestraGraph` 投影的 **wire 视图**（`client.js` 经 `useProjection('orchestraGraph')`
  读取），所以它和 `orchestrate_status` 看到的是同一份状态，且随事件自动刷新；重启后显示的是恢复出来的图。
- 面板只看：任务 id、agent_type、状态、attempts、是否可派发、报告摘要 / 诊断 / 问题条数；
  worker 的 persona 等细节留在宿主侧不下发。
- 浏览器半是**免构建的纯脚本**（`client.js`，`dsh.client.platform=web` + `immediately`）；
  面板容器继承宿主主题（`currentColor`），不引入任何样式文件或第三方依赖。
- 想关掉它：卸载插件即可（client 半随 loader 行一起消失，会话界面不受影响）。

插件还会注册一段**系统提示段**（`tool:orchestrate_plan`，order 2810），让宿主 agent 在
用户没有点名插件的大需求上也会主动走流水线——在此之前实测到的行为是"列一堆
`todo_write` 然后自己开写"。这段遵循宿主自己的惯例（workflow 占 order 2600、subagent 占
2800），用 `ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], …)` 可选注册（没有该服务的组装只损失这段倡导），
并且对**看不到 `orchestrate_plan` 的 agent 渲染成空串**——也就是每一个 worker：spawn 子代理
的 persona 只是对部署 persona 的作用域覆盖，全局提示段是会进到子代理里的。所有面向模型的
文案集中在 `src/prompts.js`。

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `orchestrate_plan` | 提交任务图（mission_brief + tasks + 可选 workers 声明）；fail-loud 校验并返回就绪集。拆解规则就写在它的 description 里：工作流只是**找**切口的手段、必须落成文件所有权，任务数按请求规模伸缩，并行写者冲突，两个拆解骨架，反模式 |
| `orchestrate_status` | 每任务一行的紧凑视图 + 当前可派发集合；无报告而失败的任务附带诊断原因 |
| `orchestrate_dispatch` | 把就绪任务 spawn 成一次性隔离 worker，阻塞等全部结算，按任务返回一行报告摘要（≤4 并发） |
| `orchestrate_review` | 对全部报告跑审核者，返回结构化判定（pass/fail + 定位到任务的问题清单） |
| `orchestrate_reroute` | 把审核问题带回 worker：任务回 pending、guidance 注入下次任务书、返回受影响下游 |
| `orchestrate_finalize` | 记录交付摘要并锁定任务图 |
| `orchestra_ping` | 存活探针 |

规划者不限于四个内置 worker 类型。`orchestrate_plan` 支持 `workers` 字段，
A 可以按任务**声明新类型**——每个声明"编程"出一个智能体规格：

```jsonc
"workers": [
  {
    "type": "ui-builder",
    "role": "你是界面构建师，专注像素级还原。",      // 身份（新类型必填）

- 任务里直接写 `"agent_type": "ui-builder"` 引用。覆盖内置类型（如 `"type": "coder"`
  且不给 role）只替换给出的部分。
- 分层保持不变：任务级 `persona` 仍叠加在声明的 role 之上，声明的 `discipline`
  永远追加——A 写不丢它。
- 审核环节不可被 plan 重新编程：审核者永远使用运营方配置的规格。
- 引擎级保证不受影响：编排工具对 worker 恒拒绝、委托深度阻止孙代理、任务是一次性隔离会话。

readme.section: 配置（worker 提示词、模型、限制）
readme.text:
**规划者自己写任务级提示词**：计划里的每个任务可带 `persona` 字段——A 为该任务定制的角色定义
（如"你是数据库迁移专家，只改 SQL 文件"）。它成为 worker 的主系统提示词，叠加在 profile 的
`discipline`（A 不可覆盖的非协商约束：researcher 不写文件、reviewer 只出判定……）之上。
`model` 与 `reasoning_effort` 同样是 A 在计划时逐任务设置的字段。

另外两种调整方式——重启 dsh 进程后生效：

1. **直接改 `src/profiles.js`**：每个角色的 `role`（身份行）、`discipline`（永久约束）、
   `effort`（`off|low|high|max`）、`toolDenyPatterns`（对宿主全局工具名做不区分大小写的
   正则匹配，命中即对该角色硬禁用）。

readme.section: 配置（worker 提示词、模型、限制）
readme.text:
2. **Config 覆盖（不改代码）**：在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`（如
   `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`）的插件条目上加 `config:` 块：

```yaml
   - id: dsh-taskforce
     name: dsh-taskforce
     config:
       taskTimeoutMs: 1200000

Config 的 `role`/`discipline`/`model`/`effort` 替换内置值；`toolDenyPatterns`
   与内置的拼接。引擎旋钮：`provider`（默认 `spawn`）、`maxConcurrentWorkers`（4）、
   `maxAttempts`（3）、`maxReviewRounds`（3）、`taskTimeoutMs`（600000）。

- **手写工具定义、近零依赖**：工具定义与 `defineTool` 编译产物同形；唯一依赖是 npm
  上的 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（用于 Config schema），pnpm 本地路径安装保持零解析负担。
- **上下文隔离**：worker 用 spawn（绝不用 fork）的一次性子智能体；上游信息只走结构化
  Report 通道，绝不携带历史。
- **提示词分层且冻结**：系统提示段管**何时**进流水线，`orchestrate_plan` 的 description 管
  **怎么拆**，参数 description 管逐字段规则——全部集中在 `src/prompts.js` 的模块常量里。
  段与工具 schema 每次请求都会重发，字节稳定的文案才保得住 provider 的前缀缓存。两段文案
  只进 A 的请求：worker 拿到空串、也看不到规划工具的 schema，所以 `TASK_ITEM_SCHEMA` 的措辞
  在 worker 轮次上零成本。离线测试对两段各设了字符预算，每请求成本不会悄悄膨胀。
- **按交付物拆，绝不按职能拆**：这段规划文案是横向调研四家 agent 系统后定稿的——Claude Code
  的 subagents、dsh 自己的 workflow/subagent 提示段、Anthropic 的多智能体研究系统、ZCode。
  没有一家按职能（UI／美术／玩法，或前端／后端）切分：都要求「一个自包含的交付物」或「按子系统
  归组」，Anthropic 还把子任务数量按请求规模伸缩而不是给死区间。原因是机制性的，不是文风问题：
  职能不拥有文件，按职能切出来的任务要么在同一个工作区里互相踩，要么只交回一段散文。所以文案把
  工作流教成**找**切口的方法，切口必须重新表述成文件所有权；同时明确禁止规划任何 worker 产不出来
  的交付物——这个宿主没有图像／音频／视频生成工具。
- **按会话分键的状态**：任务图以调用方 agent 的 session id 为键——并发会话互不串扰。
- **分层 worker 限制**：编排工具对 worker 恒拒绝；profile 的 deny 模式在派发时对宿主
  全局工具视图求交（绝不传入不存在的名字，配置错误只会静默降级而非抛错）。孙代理被
  委托深度天然阻止。**控制面工具只能按模式（pattern）拒绝**——它们不是本插件的工具，
  不同组装里未必存在；`resolveToolFilter` 一律先枚举再匹配，所以缺哪个都不会报错。
- **只用宿主的词汇落日志**：编排状态走宿主对工具调用的记录（`tool/call` + `tool/result`），
  插件侧只额外写宿
